newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's PC sales up 14 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Israel's PC sales up 14 pct in 1996.

text.p: Sales of personal computers in Israel increased by 14 percent in 1996 but growth slowed from a brisk 24 percent rise in 1995, an industry research group said on Wednesday.

The U.S.-based International Data Corporation (IDC) said 217,785 personal computers (PCs) were sold in the Jewish state in 1996, raising the value of Israel's PC market by 19 percent to $398 million against $334 million in 1995.
The growth in market value exceeded the growth in unit shipments due to the higher average selling price of PCs in 1996.
"The home market continued to lead in PC unit sales in 1996, while the business sector seems to show signs that it is reaching a point of saturation," IDC Israel's research director Sigal Hadar said.

IDC said Israel boasted the largest number of PC unit sales in the Middle East, compared to 190,000 sold in Turkey (population 60 million) and 104,000 in Saudi Arabia (population 18 million). Israel has 5.5 million residents.
